mechanism_narrative: Accelerating decline in WORKPLACES mobility (from -27.1% to -39.7% over four weeks) signals deepening workplace avoidance. This sustained contraction reduces commuter foot traffic to retail corridors, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined 12.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or WORKPLACES stabilizes above -35% for two consecutive weeks without corresponding RETAIL_REC decline.

mechanism_narrative: Severe TRANSIT contraction (from -30.1% to -40.7%) reflects public transport avoidance due to infection risk or service cuts. Reduced transit access constrains retail accessibility for non-car populations, suppressing RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -38% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -40.7% in t-0w, lowest in series
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -35% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises, or RETAIL_REC declines less than 5 percentage points from current baseline despite sustained TRANSIT depression.

mechanism_narrative: Collapsing PARKS mobility (from -5.4% to -19.9%) indicates outdoor activity suppression, signaling either policy restrictions or behavioral risk aversion. This signals broader mobility lockdown conditions that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 12.3 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS stabilizes or recovers above -15% within two weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -35%, indicating decoupling of outdoor and retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: Synchronized collapse across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RETAIL_REC (all declining 10+ points from t-2w to t-0w) indicates coordinated policy intervention (capacity restrictions, closures, or curfews). This regime will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: all three series decline simultaneously by >8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:synchronized four-week decline across all activity categories
failure_condition: Any of WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, or RETAIL_REC reverses direction and rises for two consecutive weeks, or policy announcements explicitly ease restrictions within the forecast window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 1.9% to 3.0%) coupled with collapsing RETAIL_REC (from -28.7% to -39.4%) indicates substitution of home-based activities for out-of-home consumption. This behavioral shift will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 2.5% while RETAIL_REC falls below -35%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines below 1.5% for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -25% while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, indicating behavioral reversion.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM contraction (from -7.6% to -18.1%) accelerates in parallel with RETAIL_REC decline, indicating broad consumption suppression rather than category substitution. This signals demand-side shock (income loss, confidence collapse) that will depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell 4.2 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes above -12% within two weeks while RETAIL_REC continues declining, indicating category-specific rather than demand-wide shock.

mechanism_narrative: Magnitude of RETAIL_REC decline (11 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w) exceeds all other categories, indicating retail-specific suppression beyond general mobility contraction. This accelerating retail-specific decline will continue, producing further RETAIL_REC depression over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC declines more than 8 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell 6.0 points from t-2w to t-1w and 6.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC week-on-week decline reverses to positive growth for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC stabilizes within 2 percentage points of current level for three consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Divergence between WORKPLACES decline (-39.7%) and GROCERY_PHARM decline (-18.1%) indicates essential-goods shopping persists despite workplace avoidance. If this divergence widens, essential-goods substitution will crowd out discretionary retail, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -35% while GROCERY_PHARM remains above -20%
evidence_refs: fact:21.6 percentage point gap between WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM at t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below WORKPLACES level, or RETAIL_REC rises above -30% while the WORKPLACES-GROCERY_PHARM gap remains above 15 percentage points.
